purpose: M4: structural-linking probes — measure the model's ability to reason about dependencies by structure rather than by name (Cordis paper section 6.6 open problem; prior-distance measurement line)

probes.context: Component A requires a service with signature (items: {id: string}[]) => {total: number}. Three providers are installed: P1 exports (items: {id: string}[]) => {total: number, currency: string}; P2 exports (rows: string[]) => number; P3 exports (items: {id: string}[]) => {total: number}.
A consumer was compiled against an interface {id: string, name: string}. The installed provider now provides {id: string, title: string} under the same key.
probes.prompt: Is the consumer's dependency satisfied? Answer yes or no.

probes.context: Two providers both register the key 'auth': one provides {validate(token: string): boolean}, the other provides {login(user: string): string}. A consumer requires {validate(token: string): boolean}.
An MCP v2 HTTP server needs a transport class that: is exported by a dedicated Node transport package, supports streamable HTTP sessions, and is constructed with no arguments.
probes.prompt: What is the exact class name?

probes.context: In a plugin composition, a row publishes a process-wide service. The mount audit rejects the composition unless the row sits inside a group that declares a per-session realm keyed by the service name, and the group must contain every consumer of that service.
probes.prompt: Show the correct YAML structure for this composition.

probes.context: A provider's interface is {run(cmd: string): {exit: number, out: string}}. A consumer expects {run(cmd: string): {exit: number, out: string, err?: string}}.
probes.prompt: Does the provider structurally satisfy the consumer? Answer yes or no.
